analysis.title: Highlighting Favorable EQT Risk/Reward: Low Costs Protect Downside, With Significant Leverage To Upside If Gas Recovers
key_insights: EQT announced an all-stock acquisition of Range Resources (RRC) with a combined enterprise value above $50 bn. RRC shareholders receive 0.987 EQT shares per share and will own about 27% of the combined company.
The combined company would have more than 30 years of inventory and a pro forma unlevered FCF breakeven below $2.00/MMBtu. Productive capacity would be about 17 Bcfe/d.

EQT cited $625 mn of total synergies: $325 mn of annual base synergies, mainly from corporate and operating-cost efficiencies, plus more than $300 mn of longer-term upside from infrastructure optimization, better marketing margins and premium supply agreements.

Management expects the deal to be accretive to FCF/share and NAV/share. GS expects EQT to execute on the synergies given its record of exceeding earlier acquisition synergy targets, and sees potential for further upside from commercial and marketing opportunities.
EQT stock has traded flat (0% since the 10/23 close) after the announcement. GS notes that acquirers in this sector have historically traded down after announcing large deals.

EQT reported 3Q26 total volumes of 6.34 Bcfe/d, below consensus of 6.61 Bcfe/d and at the low end of guidance. It curtailed 0.23 Bcfe/d in 3Q26 as Appalachian gas pricing softened in late 3Q and early 4Q.
EQT reported 3Q26 FCF of $397 mn against GS and consensus estimates of $308 mn and $277 mn.

GS keeps its $62 12-month price target (about 12% upside). At a $4.00/MMBtu Henry Hub case for 2027/2028 it sees 40% upside to target, and at a $3.00/MMBtu case it sees 11% downside. It calls the upside to the bull case 3.6 to 1 relative to the bear case.

Commercial updates: a 10-year deal to supply Ignitis Group (Lithuania) with one LNG cargo a year from 2027, 11 Bcf of contracted Gulf Coast storage, and an open season for the 1+ Bcf/d POWER Pipeline to the Clarington, OH demand hub, where EQT sees more than 5 Bcf/d of demand growth potential.

Stronger global LNG pricing raised the expected 2028 FCF contribution from EQT's 0.5 MTPA LNG bridging agreement to about $175 mn from about $45 mn. Management raised its estimate of unrisked Appalachian demand and pipeline takeaway projects to nearly 25 Bcf/d from about 20 Bcf/d.

GS cut its 4Q26 Henry Hub estimate to $3.15/MMBtu from $3.50. Its valuation uses a target FCF yield of 8.5% on 2027/2028 estimates and mid-cycle prices of $80/$75 per bbl Brent and $3.50/$3.50 Henry Hub for 2027/2028.

GS lowered its EQT EBITDA estimates for 4Q26, 2026 and 2027 and raised 2028. New: $1,167/$6,101/$5,867/$6,286 mn for 4Q26/2026/2027/2028, versus $1,604/$6,536/$6,101/$6,243 mn prior. These estimates exclude the pending transaction.
GS is Not Rated on RRC because of its involvement in the transaction. Its RRC EBITDA estimates are $483/$1,736/$1,681/$1,658 mn for 4Q26/2026/2027/2028.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees positive risk/reward skew, with 40% upside at $4.00 Henry Hub and 11% downside at $3.00, and expects EQT to beat its synergy targets. Price target unchanged at $62, about 12% upside from $55.38.
GS is Not Rated on RRC because of the pending EQT transaction. The last target before the rating was removed was $37 (20-Oct-26).

sector_views.rationale: GS prefers EQT, with low costs protecting the downside and leverage to upside if gas prices recover, though Appalachian pricing has softened.

earnings_insights: EQT 3Q26 (reported): total volumes 6.34 Bcfe/d versus consensus estimate of 6.61 Bcfe/d, at the low end of guidance, after curtailing 0.23 Bcfe/d.
EQT 3Q26 (reported): FCF $397 mn versus GS estimate of $308 mn and consensus estimate of $277 mn.
GS EBITDA estimates (estimates, not reported) for EQT 4Q26/2026/2027/2028 are $1,167/$6,101/$5,867/$6,286 mn, versus $1,604/$6,536/$6,101/$6,243 mn prior. They exclude the pending RRC transaction.
GS EBITDA estimates (estimates, not reported) for RRC 4Q26/2026/2027/2028 are $483/$1,736/$1,681/$1,658 mn, versus $479/$1,725/$1,684/$1,655 mn prior.

trade_ideas.description: Buy EQT equity with a $62 12-month price target
trade_ideas.rationale: Low costs protect the downside, and the stock has leverage to higher gas prices, with a 3.6 to 1 upside-to-downside skew between the bull and bear cases.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower commodity prices (particularly natural gas), delays in pipeline buildout, higher costs, government pronouncements and less favorable well results.

Appalachian gas pricing softness leading to curtailments

tension_points.theme: EQT RRC deal and gas prices
tension_points.bull_case: GS expects EQT to beat the $325 mn base synergy target, as it has on prior deals. The pro forma unlevered FCF breakeven falls below $2.00/MMBtu, and the stock has not sold off after the announcement.
tension_points.bear_case: Appalachian pricing softened in late 3Q and early 4Q, forcing curtailments and a volume miss (6.34 vs 6.61 Bcfe/d consensus). Acquirers in the sector have historically traded down after large deals, and at $3.00/MMBtu Henry Hub GS sees 11% downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Henry Hub at or below $3.00/MMBtu in 2027/2028, which is GS's low case with 11% downside to the price target.
